analysis.headline: Stocks staged their best day since April on Monday (S&P 500 +2.35%, Nasdaq +2.74%, Dow +2.15%) as oil slid on easing U.S.-Iran tensions, and this morning futures are mixed, with the Dow up and the Nasdaq-100 down, ahead of the 8:30 a.m. ET October CPI report.
analysis.summary: Monday's rally came after the S&P 500's worst week since April 2025, and it was led by semiconductors, per CNBC and the Motley Fool. The big driver was oil: Brent fell 3.6% to about $94 after President Trump said he would hold off on new strikes against Iran and Qatar brought an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Brent was trading near $91 overnight, about 22% below its Oct. 30 high. Lower oil eases the inflation worries that have kept the 10-year Treasury yield near 4.85% to 4.88% after a strong jobs report raised talk of a Fed rate hike in December; Fed Governor Waller said a 50-basis-point hike should be considered if core inflation stays elevated. Gold rose Monday (about +1.4% to roughly $4,131 in Schwab's morning snapshot) while Bitcoin slipped to about $74,700, and 24/7 Wall St. notes both have been among 2026's worst major assets as high yields and a firm dollar weigh on assets that pay no interest. Today's CPI print is the next test: economists expect a 0.3% monthly rise in headline prices and 0.2% in core, cooler than September.
drivers: Oil's slide: Brent fell 3.6% Monday to about $94 and kept falling overnight after Trump signaled a pause in military action against Iran (Oilprice.com, Globe and Mail).

Chip stocks rebounded and led the Nasdaq's 2.74% gain, while Nvidia lagged after its board opened an independent investigation tied to reports about CEO Jensen Huang (Motley Fool, Stock Titan, Nvidia).

Rate-hike worries: Friday's stronger-than-expected jobs report pushed the 10-year yield toward 4.9%, and Fed Governor Waller said a 50-basis-point December hike should be considered if core inflation stays high (Schwab, StockTwits).
Gold and Bitcoin, both down for 2026, got some support after last week's midterm results but remain pressured by high yields (Yahoo Finance, 24/7 Wall St.).
watch: Today (Tue) 8:30 a.m. ET: October CPI; consensus is +0.3% headline and +0.2% core month over month, after +0.6% and +0.3% in September (TipRanks, FXStreet).
Today (Tue) 1:00 p.m. ET: 10-year Treasury note auction (economic calendar).
Fri Nov 13, 8:30 a.m. ET: October producer price index (PPI) (economic calendar).

helium.headline: North American Helium's new Stewart Valley plant, officially opened Oct. 15 as Canada's largest helium purification facility, is ramping up just as Ottawa moves to give helium oil-and-gas-style tax treatment and helium prices run hot.
helium.summary: NAH said its Stewart Valley purification plant in southwest Saskatchewan came onstream on Sept. 20, 2026, producing about 73 million cubic feet of helium a year from a field Ryder Scott credits with 1.1 billion cubic feet of reserves, and the province says it will lift Saskatchewan's helium output by more than 40%. The project went from discovery well to production in 13 months, and local news reports a possible $100 million helium liquefier in Swift Current, which the company says is not finalized. The 2026 federal budget proposes treating helium exploration and development costs like conventional oil and gas for expenses from Nov. 5, 2026 (Prince Albert Daily Herald, Nov. 7). In the U.S. market NAH sells into, the Department of Energy named helium a critical material on Oct. 23, and law firm Mintz says spot helium prices have nearly tripled since March 2026.

realestate.headline: Portland-area home prices are holding roughly flat, with RMLS data showing an October metro median of $545,000 (up 0.9% from a year ago), while new listings shrink and mortgage rates sit just above 7%.
realestate.summary: RMLS figures summarized by RE/MAX put the Portland metro median sale price at $545,000 in October, up 0.9% from October 2025, and the year-to-date median at $549,000, down 0.2%; homes took 67 days of total market time, two fewer than a year ago, and new listings fell about 12% year over year. Redfin's city-only measure is softer, with a $518,000 median for the three months ending September, down 2.2% from a year earlier, and Realtor.com data on FRED shows a metro median listing price of $580,000 in October. Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed rate eased for a third straight week to 7.18% on Nov. 5, still well above 6.22% a year ago. On rents, CBRE says the average Portland apartment rent was about $1,764 at the end of the third quarter, up roughly 0.7% from the prior quarter, with occupancy near 95%; none of these sources broke out North Portland, St. Johns or Sauvie Island.
